stories.title: HMRC Clarifies Mandatory Tax Adviser Registration for Complex Structures
stories.summary: HMRC has published new guidance clarifying how the mandatory tax adviser registration regime applies to groups, joint ventures, partnerships and complex investment structures, confirming registration is generally not required where there is no genuine third-party advisory relationship.

stories.title: HMRC Transformation Roadmap 2026: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax Launched
stories.summary: HMRC's 2026 Transformation Roadmap update confirms the launch of Making Tax Digital for Income Tax and the publication of a final evaluation of MTD for VAT, as part of HMRC's strategy to close the tax gap through digital services.

stories.title: Taxpayers Win Entrepreneurs' Relief Case Against HMRC at First-Tier Tribunal
stories.summary: The First-Tier Tax Tribunal found in favour of taxpayers in Pontin v HMRC [2026], ruling that HMRC's contention that the qualifying conditions for Entrepreneurs' Relief were not met was incorrect.

stories.title: Government Expands Crackdown on Knife Crime with New Powers
stories.summary: The Home Office has announced an expansion of its knife crime crackdown, introducing new measures to tackle the ongoing threat of knife violence across the UK.

stories.title: 500 New Officers to Hunt Dirty Money Networks in £500m Anti-Money Laundering Strategy
stories.summary: The Home Office has launched a new Anti-Money Laundering and Asset Recovery Strategy 2026–2029, with 500 new officers to be recruited to tackle money laundering networks as part of a £500 million crackdown.

stories.title: Updated Modern Slavery Guidance Published on Victim Identification and Support
stories.summary: The Home Office has published updated statutory guidance on how to identify and support victims of modern slavery, alongside updated caseworker guidance on temporary permission to stay for trafficking victims.

stories.title: UK Statement at UN Security Council on Peace Operations
stories.summary: The UK delivered a statement at the UN Security Council affirming that the United Kingdom stands ready to work with the UN to ensure peace operations remain adaptable, effective, and fit for future challenges.

stories.title: Minister for Overseas Territories Issues Statement on Falkland Islands
stories.summary: The FCDO Minister for Overseas Territories published a statement on 18 September regarding the Falkland Islands, covering the UK's ongoing commitment to the territory and its residents.

stories.title: UK ODA Spend 2025: Final Statistics Published
stories.summary: FCDO published the final statistics on the UK's Official Development Assistance spend for 2025, providing transparency on how UK international aid was allocated across global programmes.

stories.title: Winter Fuel Payment Claim Form Updated for 2026
stories.summary: DWP has updated the Winter Fuel Payment claim form, reflecting the latest eligibility criteria and application process for the upcoming winter season.

stories.title: Small Pots Pension Consolidation Consultation Launched
stories.summary: DWP has opened a consultation titled 'Small Pots: A Pathway for Consolidation', seeking views on how to tackle the growing problem of small pension pots left behind by workers who change jobs frequently.

stories.title: Timms Review September 2026 Update: PIP Reform Progress
stories.summary: The co-chairs of the Timms Review published their September update on reform of Personal Independence Payment (PIP), following the July 2026 report which found the current system 'not fit for purpose'.

stories.title: 25-Year Farming Roadmap Launched: New Plan for Profitable and Sustainable English Agriculture
stories.summary: DEFRA's Environment Secretary Emma Reynolds launched the 25-year Farming Roadmap ('Farming Roadmap 2050: Growing England's Future'), the most significant commitment to English farming since World War II, providing farmers long-term certainty beyond the next harvest.

stories.title: Family Food FYE 2025 Statistics Published
stories.summary: DEFRA has published the Family Food statistics for the financial year ending 2025, providing data on household food expenditure, consumption patterns, and nutritional trends across the UK.

stories.title: Farming Annual Report 2025-2026 Published
stories.summary: DEFRA has published its Farming Annual Report for 2025-2026, documenting the progress on agricultural policy delivery, Environmental Land Management schemes, and farm support payments across England.

stories.title: Veterans to Be Mobilised to Test UK's War Resilience in 2027 Exercise
stories.summary: The MoD announced that some veterans from the UK's strategic reserve of ~95,000 retired officers will be called up as part of a major 2027 war resilience exercise, with Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones saying it will challenge the MoD 'on a scale we haven't seen for a very long time'.

stories.title: UK Armed Forces Step Up Monitoring of Increased Russian Activity in UK Waters
stories.summary: Royal Navy warships and helicopters spent 21 days on operations monitoring Russian naval activity in UK waters and the North Atlantic throughout July, with the MoD highlighting the heightened surveillance operation.

stories.title: British Weapons Jobs Rise by More Than 50% in a Year
stories.summary: Defence investment is strengthening the UK industrial base, with British weapons manufacturing jobs rising by more than 50% year-on-year as the government's Defence Investment Plan begins to take effect.

agencies.name: BIST
agencies.description: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

stories.title: Government Moves to Acquire Speciality Steel UK
stories.summary: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds announced the government will work towards a public acquisition of Speciality Steel UK (SSUK), in a move to protect the strategic UK speciality steel industry and its workforce.

stories.title: UK-Switzerland Enhanced Free Trade Agreement Negotiations Update
stories.summary: BIST published an update on the UK-Switzerland enhanced free trade agreement negotiations, alongside the latest UK trade in numbers and core statistics book showing the state of UK trade and investment.

stories.title: Flexible Working Consultation Outcome Published
stories.summary: BIST published the outcome of the 'Make Work Pay: Improving Access to Flexible Working' consultation, setting out the government's approach to expanding flexible working rights for employees across UK businesses.

stories.title: Major Expansion of NHS Mental Health Support: 159 New Centres Backed by £343m
stories.summary: The government announced 100 new community mental health centres and 59 new mental health emergency departments across England, funded by £343 million, representing the biggest redesign of mental health services in a generation. The first sites open from autumn 2026.

stories.title: GP Patient Data Being Added to NHS Federated Data Platform
stories.summary: A new NHS pilot is adding GP practice patient data to the NHS Federated Data Platform (FDP), expanding the platform's reach beyond hospitals to include primary care data for improved analytics and care coordination.

stories.title: NHS Modernisation Bill 2026-27 Progressing Through Parliament
stories.summary: The Health Bill 2026-27 (NHS Modernisation Bill), which provides the legal basis for the largest NHS reorganisation in over a decade including the abolition of NHS England as a separate body, continues its parliamentary progress with a new research briefing published.

stories.title: Royal Mail Service Disruptions at 13 Delivery Offices This Weekend
stories.summary: Royal Mail's service update lists 13 delivery offices affected by disruptions on Saturday 19 and Sunday 20 September, including sites in Ballycastle, Bicester, Chichester, Reading, Wandsworth, and Wilmslow, among others.

stories.title: Royal Mail Staff Say They Were Told to Hide Post to Make Targets Look Met
stories.summary: A BBC investigation revealed that postal workers across the UK were regularly instructed to 'take the mail for a ride' — hiding undelivered letters from inspectors — while Royal Mail bosses were called to Parliament to answer questions about ongoing postal delays.
